caption: Two masses sit on a rod, spinning around a pivot. Slide them outward, the spin slows down. Slide them back in, it speeds up again.  Nothing about the masses changed. Nothing about the rod changed. Only their distance from the pivot changed. And that alone is enough to change how the whole system resists being spun.  That resistance has a name: moment of inertia.  #physics #mechanics #stem #rotation #math

Take a biconvex lens and slice it horizontally, right through the optical axis. Two halves fall apart, a top half and a bottom half. Each one is still a working lens. Full lens: Rays from the object tip converge to form the real, inverted, diminished image. Top half only: Rays enter only through the upper half. The optical element is now decentered above the axis, so the whole converging bundle drifts down.  Bottom half only: The mirror case. Rays enter only through the lower half and the bundle drifts up.  #physics #optics #lens #optical #stem

Tilt a mirror by a small angle, and the reflected ray swings twice as far.  That's the 2θ rule, and it's exact, not approximate.  Rotate the mirror by 10° and the reflected ray turns 20°. Rotate by 20° and the ray turns 40°. The relationship is always θ_mirror : θ_ray = 1 : 2.  #physics #optics #lightreflection #stem #math

Heat a gas while the pressure is held constant, and it does the only thing it can: it expands.  The piston is free to move, so nothing resists the gas as it warms. Every bit of added heat turns into volume growth, the gas pushes the piston outward instead of building up pressure. That's what "isobaric" means: same pressure, changing everything else.  #physics #thermodynamics #thermal #stem #math

Convex mirrors diverge light.  Send parallel rays at one and they bounce off the curved surface and spread apart. Send rays aimed at F, C, or the vertex, same story. After reflection, nothing converges in front of the mirror.  But look behind the mirror. The dashed backward extensions of those same rays converge at a single point. That point is the virtual image.  #physics #optics #optical #stem #math

Put a wire in a magnetic field, send current through it, and the wire jumps.  Not toward the field. Not along the wire. Perpendicular to both.  That's the vector cross product:  F = I L × B  With the field pointing into the page and current flowing right, the right-hand rule puts the force straight up. Reverse the current and it snaps down,  because flipping I flips the cross product.  #physics #magnetism #stem #electromagnetism #math

White light in. Rainbow out. Every colour inside white light bends by a different amount. Red bends the least, violet bends the most. That's because the refractive index of glass depends on wavelength, a fact called dispersion.  #physics #stem #optics #optical #math

An object sits beyond the center of curvature of a concave mirror. Three rays leave its tip and strike the mirror.  Each one follows a rule:  A ray parallel to the axis reflects through the focus. A ray through the focus reflects parallel to the axis. A ray through the center of curvature reflects straight back.  After reflection, all three cross at one point, the image. It's real (the rays actually meet), inverted (points downward), and diminished (half the object's height). It forms between C and F.  #physics #optics #lightrays #stem #optical

Place a positive charge somewhere. Its field lines stream outward in every direction, running off to infinity. There's nowhere else for them to go.  Now place a negative charge nearby. Suddenly those same lines have somewhere to end. They bend, curve, sweep around the outside, and terminate on the negative charge from every direction, even from behind it.  The result is a closed system of field lines. Nothing escapes. Nothing appears from nowhere. Everything that leaves the positive charge arrives at the negative one.  #physics #stem #math #physicsanimation #physicsreels

Two opposite charges, one field.  Every line leaves the positive charge and lands on the negative one.  Notice too how the field spreads. Near the charges, lines are tightly packed and the field is strong. Far away, they thin out, because field strength falls as one over distance squared. The density of lines is the field strength.  The two straight horizontal lines running off to the left and right are the axial field lines, the special ones that don't loop back, because they mathematically extend to infinity before returning.  #physics #stem #electrostatic #electricfield #math

Two like charges push each other away. Move them apart, and the force doesn't just weaken, it collapses fast. Double the distance, and the force drops to a quarter. Triple it, and it falls to a ninth. That's the inverse-square law, and it governs every electric interaction in the universe.  #physics #electromagnetism #stem #electrostatics #math

Two charged spheres. Different charges. One touches the other.  Charge flows from the higher-charged sphere to the lower-charged one, until both settle at the same value. The individual charges changed. Their sum did not.  #physics #charge #stem #electrostatics #electron

No heat enters. No heat leaves. Just work. A gas is compressed inside a perfectly insulated cylinder. Since Q = 0, every joule of work done on the gas has to go somewhere, and it goes straight into internal energy. The gas heats up. Molecules visibly speed up. The glow shifts from cool blue to warm orange.  Then the piston reverses and the gas expands. Work is done by the gas, its internal energy drops, and it cools back down.  On the P-V diagram below, the trail traces the adiabatic curve, sitting above the dashed isothermal reference.  #physics #thermodynamics #thermal #stem #physicsanimation

The most boring dot in the animation is the most important one.  When two pucks collide on a frictionless table, the individual velocities change dramatically. One puck that was drifting right now shoots left. The other that was heading left now races right. Kinetic energy redistributes. Trails bend. Directions flip. But the center of mass, the mass-weighted average position of the whole system, carries on completely undisturbed. Straight line. Constant speed. Before, during, after.  #physics #stem #kinematics #collision #math

Two blocks on a massless rod. One heavy, one light.  Where does the system balance? Not at the midpoint. Closer to the heavier block. That's the center of mass:    x_cm = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂) / (m₁ + m₂)  #physics #mechanics #stem #math #classicalmechanics

Heat one junction. Cool the other. A voltage appears across the wire.  That's the Seebeck effect, the principle behind every thermocouple, every radioisotope generator, every waste-heat recovery system.  Watch the voltmeter climb as the flame rises. The junction glows red, the other frosts blue, and a steady current begins circulating through the loop. Remove the heat, and the voltage fades.  #physics #stem #thermal #thermocouple #thermodynamics

Two identical cylinders. Two identical gases. Two pistons pushed in at exactly the same speed. The only difference: one cylinder is insulated, the other sits in a heat bath.  ADIABATIC (left): Insulated walls. Q = 0. Every joule of work stays trapped in the gas, so the temperature climbs. PV^γ = const  ISOTHERMAL (right): Heat bath attached. T = const. Excess energy leaks out as fast as it's generated, so the temperature holds steady. PV = const  #physics #thermal #thermodynamics #stem #math

Same compression. Same starting gas. Two completely different outcomes.   Left: Adiabatic Insulated walls. Q = 0. Every bit of work goes into the gas, so it heats up. Temperature climbs from 1.00 to 2.02 × T₀.  Right: Isothermal Heat bath attached. T stays constant. Extra energy leaks out as fast as it's generated, so the gas stays cool.   #physics #thermodynamics #stem #thermal #math

Two different gases mix → entropy rises. Two same gases mix → nothing happens. Same equation. Same setup. Opposite answer. This is Gibbs' paradox, and it's hiding one of the deepest ideas in physics: entropy counts distinguishable arrangements.  #physics #thermodynamics #stem #entropy #math

Heat flows in one direction. Always.  This animation starts with two chambers: hot gas on the left at 800 K, cold gas on the right at 200 K, separated by a partition. Remove the partition, and watch what happens.  Before mixing: The hot particles jiggle fast. The cold particles drift slowly. Particle speed scales as √T, so the temperature difference is visible in every bounce.  During mixing: Hot particles wander right, cold particles wander left. Their speeds converge and the temperature bars on both sides move toward each other.  After equilibrium: Both chambers settle at the same temperature 500 K. Every particle moves at the same average speed. The entropy readout climbs from 0 to +2.50 k_B and stops. It never goes down.  #physics #thermodynamics #entropy #stem #math

The First Law of Thermodynamics says energy can’t be created or destroyed, only converted.  Isochoric heating (A → B) Volume locked. Heat goes in, pressure rises, temperature climbs. W = 0, so Q = ΔU.  Isothermal expansion (B → C) Temperature held constant while the gas expands. ΔU = 0, so Q = W — all the heat becomes work.  Adiabatic expansion (C → D) No heat in or out. The gas does work, so it cools. Q = 0, so ΔU = –W.  Isochoric cooling (D → A) Volume locked again. Heat leaves, pressure drops, temperature falls. W = 0, so Q = ΔU.  #physics #thermodynamics #stem #thermal #math

Thank you for 1M views 🥹❤️  No heat enters or leaves the insulated cylinder, so all the work goes into changing the gas’s internal energy.  Compress: work is done ON the gas → molecules speed up → temperature rises. Expand: gas does work → molecules slow down → temperature drops.  The glowing trail follows the adiabatic curve: PVᵞ = constant, with γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas. The dashed blue curve is the isothermal reference (PV = constant). Notice how the adiabatic curve is steeper.  #physics #thermodynamics #stem #thermal #math

Add more gas, the volume grows. Remove gas, it shrinks. At constant pressure and temperature, volume is directly proportional to the number of moles — that's Avogadro's Law, one face of the Ideal Gas Law. Watch the piston rise and fall as n sweeps from 0.5 to 3.0 mol, and notice the last line of the table: P·V / (n·T) never changes. It's always 8.314 — the gas constant R. Four variables. One equation. One universal constant.  #physics #thermodynamics #stem #math #kineticenergy

Heat a gas. It expands. Cool it. It shrinks.  That simple fact is Charles's Law, discovered in 1787 by Jacques Charles, a French physicist who noticed that every gas expands by the same fraction for the same temperature rise.  The top panel shows a freely moving piston. As the gas warms, the molecules speed up, the piston rises, and the gas glows warmer.  The bottom panel tells the deeper story: plot volume against Kelvin temperature and you get a perfect straight line, one that, when extended backward, points straight at absolute zero.  #physics #thermodynamics #stem #idealgas #math

Boyle's Law: Pressure × Volume = Constant   Push a piston down, the pressure rises. Pull it up, the pressure falls. But multiply them — and you always get the same number. That's Boyle's Law. For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature: P · V = k  Top panel: a glass cylinder containing gas molecules. A metallic piston compresses the gas, then releases it, then compresses it again. As the volume shrinks, the gas shifts toward a warmer orange and the pressure arrow inside grows.  Bottom panel: the P–V curve traced live. Each compression and expansion draws a point on the classic hyperbola P=k/V.  #physics #thermodynamics #stem #math #physicsanimation

Ball Bouncing on a Spring: Energy in Motion   A ball falls onto a spring. Gravity gives it kinetic energy. The spring absorbs that energy, compresses, and gives it all back. The ball flies up to exactly the same height.  Nothing is lost. Energy just keeps changing its form.  Top panel: the physical system. The ball falls under gravity, hits the plate, compresses the spring, and rebounds.  Bottom panel: the energy breakdown in real time:  🔹Gravitational PE = mgy 🔹 Spring PE = ½k(L₀ − y)² 🔹 Kinetic energy = ½mv²  #physics #stem #math #classicalmechanics #calculus

Collision in a Box: 2D Ideal Gas  Forty spheres. One square box. Every collision elastic. This is a molecular-dynamics view of an ideal gas.  What you see:  🔹Every ball–ball collision is perfectly elastic: momentum is conserved, and so is kinetic energy.  🔹The KE equation at the top — KE = Σ ½ mᵢ vᵢ² — stays constant throughout. The live HUD in the top-right proves it: the total kinetic energy stays locked at 100%, second after second.  🔹Wall hit counters on all four sides tick upward as balls strike the walls. That's the microscopic origin of pressure: molecules hitting a surface and exchanging momentum.  🔹Speed and direction get redistributed constantly through collisions — but the total energy never changes.  #physics #stem #collision #kineticenergy #chemistry

Perfectly Inelastic Collision: Two Soft Bodies Merge   Two soft deformable balls collide head-on. Momentum is conserved. Kinetic energy is not.  🔵 Case I — Equal masses. The two balls meet, squash at contact, and merge into a single body that gradually settles into a flatter, wider shape. 🟠 Case II — Unequal masses (1 : 4). The heavier ball dominates the motion; both balls deform, and the merged pair drifts forward together at the centre-of-mass velocity.  Why this happens — in a perfectly inelastic collision, both bodies share the same final velocity: the centre-of-mass velocity. The "missing" kinetic energy becomes heat, sound, and permanent deformation of the soft material.  #physics #stem #classicalmechanics #collision #math

Off-Centre Collision: The Physics of Scattering Two balls approach each other off-centre. They don't swap velocities — they scatter at an angle. This is what happens when the collision is oblique rather than head-on.  Watch three classic mass ratios play back to back:  🔵 Equal masses — the balls scatter symmetrically, forming a clean "V" shape. 🟠 Heavy hits light — the heavy ball plows forward, while the light ball shoots off at a wide angle. 🔴 Light hits heavy — the light ball bounces back, the heavy ball barely nudges forward.  #physics #stem #classicalmechanics #collision #math

Elastic Collision of Two Masses ⚪⚫  Two balls. One collision. Both momentum and kinetic energy conserved. This is an elastic collision — the purest kind of impact in classical mechanics.  Watch three classic cases play back to back:  🔵 Equal masses — the balls simply swap velocities. Nothing else changes. 🟠 Heavy hits light — the heavy ball plows forward, the light one shoots off fast. Both end up moving in the same direction. 🔴 Light hits heavy — the light ball bounces back, the heavy one barely nudges forward.  #physics #stem #classicalmechanics #collision #math

Bouncing Ball with Restitution 🏀  Drop a ball. It hits the ground and bounces back — but never to the same height. Each bounce is a fraction of the previous one.  🔵 Top panel: the real bounce — a rigid ball falling and rebounding. 🟠 Bottom panel: the height vs time graph. Each segment is a parabola. As the ball bounces, the peaks shrink and the parabolas get narrower.  Each rebound speed is multiplied by the restitution coefficient e (here e = 0.82). So each bounce height is e² ≈ 0.67 of the previous one. Watch the peaks shrink geometrically — a perfect visual of exponential decay.  #physics #classicalmechanics #stem #calculus #math

Four balls. Same speed. Same instant. Different angles.  Watch how the story unfolds:  The 75° ball launches almost straight up — dramatic, airborne, but lands close.  The 30° ball flies flat and fast — quick to land, moderate range.  The 45° ball finds the balance — it sails the farthest of all.  The 60° ball mirrors the 30° ball — landing at exactly the same spot.  That's sin(2θ) at work. It peaks at 45° and is symmetric around it, so complementary angles always produce the same range.  #physics #math #stem #classicalmechanics #physicsanimation

The Astroid: Envelope of a Sliding Segment ✨  Slide a line segment of fixed length with its endpoints on the axes. Its envelope traces out a four‑cusped curve — the astroid.  🔵 Upper panel: the sliding segment in motion, with 24 faint copies showing the family of all such segments. Their envelope is exactly the astroid. 🟠 Lower panel: the parametric curve x = a·cos³t, y = a·sin³t, traced out step by step.  #math #mathart #stem #mathanimation #astroid

Growth That Slows Down: The Gompertz Curve  Rises slowly. Accelerates. Then saturates gradually. This is the Gompertz curve, and it's one of the most useful growth curves in science.  🔵 Upper panel (k = 1): a gentle S‑curve that rises smoothly from 0 to 1. 🟠 Lower panel (k = 5): a sharper S‑curve, reaching saturation much sooner.  #math #mathart #stem #mathanimation #mathisbeautiful

Interference of Waves 🌊  Two identical waves meet. Their sum depends entirely on the phase difference φ.  🔵 Top panel: both waves shown together.  • Cyan = wave 1  • Amber (dashed) = wave 2, shifted by φ  🟣 Bottom panel: the sum y₁ + y₂, the actual result of interference.  Watch what happens as φ sweeps from 0 to 2π:    φ = 0 → fully constructive. The waves align and the sum doubles.  φ = π → fully destructive. The waves oppose and the sum vanishes.  In between → partial interference.  This is the physics behind:    Noise-cancelling headphones 🎧  Anti-reflective coatings on lenses 🌈  Thin-film colours on soap bubbles 🫧  The double-slit experiment ⚛️  Phased-array radar and 5G antennas 📡  #physics #math #stem #interference #waves

Frequency Modulation – Encoding Information in Frequency 📡  A slow wave controls the frequency of a fast one. This is FM.  🔵 Top panel: the modulating signal – a slow, smooth wave that carries the message. 🟠 Middle panel: the instantaneous frequency – the carrier frequency wobbling around its base value. 🟣 Bottom panel: the FM signal itself. When the instantaneous frequency is high, the oscillations are dense. When it's low, they spread out.  The equation is f(t) = sin(ωt + A·sin(ω_m·t)), where ω is the carrier frequency, ω_m is the modulating frequency, and A controls the depth of the frequency deviation.  This simple idea is the foundation of:  FM radio 📻  Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth 📶  Digital communication systems 🌐  Many forms of radar and telemetry 📡  #physics #math #stem #frequencymodulation #mathart

The Pendulum: Motion, Gravity, and a Perfect Cosine 🕰️  A pendulum swinging under gravity – rendered with a metallic rod and a shaded spherical bob.  🔵 Upper panel: the pendulum swings back and forth, tracing a smooth arc around its equilibrium position.  🟠 Lower panel: the angle θ(t) plotted against time. The motion is a pure cosine – smooth, periodic, and predictable.  The swing is governed by θ(t) = θ₀ cos(√(g/L)·t), where g is gravity and L is the length of the rod. Change the length, and the rhythm changes. Change gravity, and the rhythm changes again.  This is one of the simplest and most elegant systems in classical mechanics – a perfect introduction to oscillation and periodicity.  #physics #pendulum  #stem #math #oscillation

Turbulence: Every Term Adds a Sharper Ripple  Add a fast ripple, then a faster one, then a faster one — each half the size of the last. The result is a curve that looks rough at every scale. That's turbulence: structure that never smooths out, no matter how far you zoom in.  #math #physics #stem #mathart #turbulence

The Dawson Function: A Tug of War Between Growth and Decay  Take an exponentially growing integral, multiply it by a Gaussian decay, and you get one of the most elegant special functions in mathematics.  🔵 Upper panel: the Dawson function F(t) – an odd bell that peaks near t ≈ 0.92 and then slowly fades like 1/(2t). The dashed grey line shows that asymptotic tail. 🟠 Lower panel: the two competing factors. • Cyan: e^(−t²), the Gaussian decay. • Amber: ∫₀ᵗ e^(s²) ds, the growing integral (normalised for comparison).  #math #calculus #stem #mathart #mathanimation

Cauchy‑Damped Oscillation: A Sine Inside a Lorentzian 🌊  A sine wave wrapped in a Lorentzian envelope. The result is a symmetric pulse that rings briefly and fades smoothly on both sides.  🔵 Upper panel (γ = 2): a tight, short‑lived pulse – the oscillation dies out quickly. 🟠 Lower panel (γ = 8): a wide, lingering ring – the oscillation survives much longer.  #math #physics #stem #mathart #mathanimation

The Logistic Function: From Gentle Curve to Sharp Step  One simple formula, two very different behaviours.  🔵 Upper panel (k = 1): a soft, wide S‑curve. Slow to rise, slow to saturate – the classic sigmoid shape. 🟠 Lower panel (k = 10): a nearly sharp step. The curve snaps from 0 to 1 almost instantly around t = 0.  #math #mathart #stem #mathanimation #physics

One simple formula, two very different personalities.  🔵 Upper panel (k = 1): a soft, sine‑like wave – smooth and rounded. 🟠 Lower panel (k = 10): a nearly square wave with gently rounded corners – crisp and snappy.  The trick is tanh – the hyperbolic tangent. For small k, it barely changes the sine. For large k, it pushes the curve toward ±1, creating a square wave without sharp discontinuities.  #math #physics #stem #mathart #mathanimation

Nested Composition: A Quadratic Pulse as Frequency 🌊  Take a smooth quadratic pulse, use it as the frequency of a sine wave, and you get a "whoosh" – the oscillation speeds up and slows down predictably.  🔵 Upper panel: the frequency pulse f(t) – a gentle bump that rises from 1 Hz to 8 Hz and back. 🟠 Lower panel: the resulting chirp y(t) – the wave starts with wide loops, becomes dense and fast in the middle, then relaxes back to wide loops.  #math #physics #stem #mathart #frequency

Same waveform, two very different exponents.  🔵 Upper panel (p = 2): a soft, parabolic coast – the curve stays high for a while before gently falling. 🟠 Lower panel (p = 20): an extremely sharp spike, then a long flat tail – almost like a real sawtooth.  #math #physics  #stem #mathart #physicsanimation

A fast wave multiplied by another close frequency creates a slow pulsing beat that fades over time.  The fast wiggles come from the sum of the two frequencies, while the slow swell comes from their tiny difference.  #physics #math #stem #mathart #physicsanimation

Two high frequencies (100 and 101) create a dense vibration, but their tiny difference produces a slow, pulsing beat that decays over time. Fast wiggles, slow heartbeat, fading to silence.  #physics #math #stem #mathart #oscillation

The Damped Beat: A Decaying Pulsation 🔊  Watch the sum of two close frequencies – ω₁ = 10 and ω₂ = 11 – interfere, creating a classic beat pattern that slowly fades away.  🔵 The amplitude swells and shrinks (the "wah‑wah" effect) while the overall intensity decays exponentially. 🔴 The dashed envelope shows the decay boundary – the sound fades to silence over time.  #physics #oscillation #stem #math #mathart

Sound Waves in Motion – Compression & Rarefaction 🔊  Watch a longitudinal sound wave travel through a medium, particle by particle.  🔵 Compression – particles bunch together (blue, forward displacement) 🔴 Rarefaction – particles spread apart (red, backward displacement)  The upper panel shows the particles moving horizontally, while the lower panel shows the displacement curve – peaks correspond to compression, troughs to rarefaction.  This is how sound propagates – not by transporting matter, but by passing energy through a chain of vibrating particles.  #physics #waves #stem #physicsanimation #soundwaves

A Heart Drawn by Math ❤️  Watch a perfect heart shape emerge from a simple parametric curve – drawn stroke by stroke, then filled with a warm glow.  🔴 The curve traces out a classic heart, elegant and symmetrical. 💕 A soft red shadow fills the interior as the shape completes.  Math isn’t just numbers – it’s art, emotion, and beauty. This heart was born from equations, but it speaks the universal language of love.  #math #mathart #stem #mathanimation #MathIsBeautiful

The Gamma Function: Smoothly Interpolating Factorials   Watch the Gamma function Γ(z) evolve along the line z = a + i·0.5 as a increases from 0.1 to 5.0.  🔵 Top: Real part of Γ(z) – showing the smooth, oscillatory behavior that connects integer factorial values. 🟣 Bottom: Imaginary part of Γ(z) – the companion oscillation that arises from the complex nature of the function.  The Gamma function is the continuous generalization of the factorial: Γ(n+1) = n! for integer n. Animating it in the complex plane reveals the beautiful, smooth interpolation between these discrete values.  #math #mathart #stem #calculus #physics

Quantum Scattering: Wave Packet Meets a Delta Potential  Watch a quantum wave packet approach a delta potential barrier at x=0 – and see it split into reflected and transmitted parts.  🔵 Top: Probability density |ψ|² – the packet travels from left to right, hits the narrow barrier, and partially reflects while partially transmitting through. 🟣 Bottom: The real (cyan) and imaginary (pink) parts of the wavefunction – showing the oscillatory structure and the phase changes during scattering.  The delta barrier is shown as a thin yellow line at x=0. The live readout in the top-left corner tracks the transmitted (T) and reflected (R) probabilities – and their sum remains exactly 1, confirming probability conservation.  #physics #quantumphysics #stem #waves #physicsanimation

Growing Oscillations: Exponential vs Super‑Exponential Growth 🚀  Watch two oscillatory functions with positive exponents – the amplitude grows as x increases.  Top: exponential growth. The oscillations become increasingly dramatic, with a steady, predictable rise.  Bottom: super‑exponential growth. The amplitude explodes far more rapidly, dwarfing the exponential case.  This is the opposite of damping – it’s growth driven by positive exponents. The difference between eˣ and eˣ² becomes dramatic as x increases.  #math #oscillation #stem #physics #mathart

Damped Oscillations: Exponential vs Gaussian   Watch two damped oscillatory functions side by side – both with the same rapid oscillations (cos 20x), but different decay envelopes.  #math #Oscillations #physics #stem #mathart

Chirped Gaussian Wave Packet  Watch a Gaussian wave packet with a quadratic phase (a "chirp") evolve in free space.  🔹 The initial packet has a phase that varies quadratically with position, so the local frequency changes linearly across the packet – that’s the chirp. 🔹 As time passes, the packet spreads, and the chirp causes the oscillations to speed up or slow down depending on where you look.  This is a fundamental concept in signal processing, optics, and quantum mechanics – where a wave can carry a "frequency sweep."  #physics #quantumphysics #stem #waves #math

Damped Oscillations with a Twist – e⁻ˣ sin(1/x)   Watch the function f(x) = e⁻ˣ sin(1/x) draw itself from near zero to the right.  🔹 As x → 0, the oscillations become infinitely rapid – a beautiful mathematical singularity. 🔹 The exponential decay e⁻ˣ acts as an envelope, damping the wiggles as x increases.  #math #mathanimation #stem #mathart #oscillation

Resonance: When the Driving Frequency Matches the Natural Frequency   Watch a driven harmonic oscillator as the driving frequency ω_d sweeps from below to above the natural frequency ω₀ = 1.0 (with light damping γ = 0.1).  🔵 Top: Displacement x(t) – the amplitude grows dramatically as ω_d approaches ω₀, then decays again. 🟠 Bottom: Driving force F₀ cos(ω_d t) – shown as a dashed line for reference.  The yellow marker at the bottom shows the current driving frequency. At resonance, the amplitude reaches its maximum.  This is the same principle behind:  🔹A swing pushed at just the right rhythm 🎠  🔹A singer shattering a glass with their voice 🎤  🔹Tuning a radio to a station 📻  Resonance is everywhere and it’s beautiful.  #physics #oscillation #stem #physicsanimation #math

Energy Decay in a Damped Oscillator   🔵 Top panel: Displacement x(t) – the oscillations decay exponentially. 🟢 Bottom panel: Kinetic (cyan), potential (magenta), and total (white) energy over time.  As the oscillator loses energy to friction, the total energy decays exponentially. Meanwhile, kinetic and potential energies continuously exchange – peaking when the other is zero.  This is the energy budget of a damped system:  🔹Kinetic energy is maximum at equilibrium. 🔹Potential energy is maximum at turning points. 🔹Total energy gradually decreases, dissipated by damping.  #physics #oscillation #stem #physicsanimation #math

From Oscillations to Overdamping  Watch a damped harmonic oscillator transition through three distinct regimes as the damping coefficient γ increases from 0.2 to 2.5.  🔵 Underdamped (γ < 1): The system oscillates with exponentially decaying amplitude – think of a swing with air resistance. 🟣 Critically damped (γ = 1): The fastest return to equilibrium without any overshoot – perfect for shock absorbers and door closers. 🟠 Overdamped (γ > 1): The system slowly returns to rest without oscillating – like a heavy door with thick oil.  #physics #oscillation #stem #physicsanimation #math

Damped Harmonic Oscillator – Decaying Oscillations  The main curve (pink) shows the position x(t) as it oscillates with exponentially decaying amplitude. The dashed envelopes (pink) show the decay boundaries ±Ae⁻ᵞᵗ. This is the classic model for a mass on a spring with friction, or an LCR circuit – ubiquitous in physics and engineering.  #physics #oscillation #stem #physicsanimation #math

Gaussian Distribution – The Bell Curve  Watch the classic bell curve change its shape as the standard deviation (σ) increases from 0.3 to 2.5.   The curve is drawn live for σ = 0.3, then σ smoothly grows.  The shaded region marks the area between μ − σ and μ + σ.  The 2σ label inside the curve shows the full width of the central region.  This is the Gaussian (normal) distribution – the backbone of statistics, probability, and data science.  #math #mathart #stem #physics #statistics

Quantum Tunneling – Wave Packet Scattering  Watch a quantum wave packet approach a potential barrier – and tunnel through!   👉Top: Probability density |ψ|² – the packet splits into a reflected part (moving left) and a transmitted part (moving right).  👉Bottom: The real and imaginary parts of the wavefunction – showing the oscillatory structure and the exponential decay inside the barrier.  The barrier height V₀ = 1.0 is higher than the particle’s energy Eₖ = 0.32, so classically it would be completely reflected. But in quantum mechanics, there’s a finite probability to tunnel through – here about 18% (shown as T in the top‑right corner).  This is one of the most iconic phenomena in quantum physics – and a beautiful demonstration of the wave nature of matter.  #physics #quantumphysics #quantumtunneling #stem #physicsanimation

The Boltzmann Distribution — A Window into Thermal Physics  This animation visualizes the Boltzmann distribution, one of the most fundamental equations in statistical mechanics. It tells us how energy is distributed among particles in a system at thermal equilibrium.  The Physics:    Cold temperatures (low T): Most particles are frozen in the ground state (low energy).
